answer: Arrival-Spread Admission: each new identity must survive a randomized probe window before it can send traffic. Admitted agents get a slow-start allowance; a probe arriving too early or too clustered triggers an echo check against prior arrival timestamps, and repeat collisions push the identity past a comet threshold into quarantine, resetting its window. An attacker must hold each identity idle through many full windows and stagger launches across the horizon, converting cheap mass registration into sustained waiting cost per identity.
